title: Likely 5.1.1 rejection: the privacy policy never confirms that the outside services it names protect data as well as the policy does, which Apple lists as a must
evidence: developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines (Last Updated: October 16, 2026), 5.1.1(i): 'The privacy policy must clearly and explicitly: ... Confirm that any third party with whom an app shares user data ... will provide the same or equal protection of user data as stated in the app's privacy policy'. grep -i 'equal|same protection' on docs/store/privacy.html and the live page: no such sentence; the 'Who else receives data' section lists Open Food Facts, Anthropic, Overpass, Cloudflare, Apple, RevenueCat without it. The other 5.1.1(i) points (what is collected, retention, revoking consent, deletion) are present.
fix: One sentence in the 'Who else receives data' section, EN and FR, e.g. 'Pexi shares data only with the services named here, each bound by its own terms to protect it at least as well as this policy does' (true once the transfer assessments in legal review question 3 are on file); publish with the item above

title: The privacy manifest leaves out the file-timestamp reason that the Filesystem plugin's own instructions say the app must declare
evidence: native/node_modules/@capacitor/filesystem/README.md:16-20: 'you must create a PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy ... the required dictionary key is NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp and the recommended reason is C617.1'; plugin source reads creation and modification dates (IONFileStructures+Converters.swift:45-46); native/ios/App/App/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy has an empty NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes array. Builds 2 to 9 processed, so Apple's upload check has not blocked it so far; Camera, Haptics, TextZoom, in-app-review and secure-storage plugins ship no manifest (find count 0) and their iOS sources call no required-reason API (grep).
fix: Add one NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes entry: NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp with reason C617.1

title: The camera permission text promises photographs the app no longer takes, and calls Pexi 'This app'
evidence: Info.plist NSCameraUsageDescription: 'This app uses the camera to scan barcodes and photograph items so it can look up the price.'; the shopper photo path is off (FLAGS.photoId false, listing.md:72; camera frames stay on the phone, dev-mode.js header). title: Usage tracking has no off switch, while 5.1.1(ii) asks for an easy way to withdraw consent
evidence: Guideline 5.1.1(ii): 'Apps must also provide the customer with an easily accessible and understandable way to withdraw consent.' Policy: 'This is recorded whether or not you have turned location on'; listing.md:77 'Not gated by any consent: track.js has no consent check.' Withdrawal today is only the Delete my data email. Rejections on this point are uncommon (assumed).
fix: A 'Share usage data' switch on the You screen (on by default) that stops track.js batches, plus one policy line
